faq: Which form tools do you connect?
Google Forms, Typeform, Jotform, Tally, Wix forms, WordPress form plugins and many others. If your form can send data when submitted, we can usually receive it.
Which places can the data go?
Google Sheets, Excel online, Airtable, Notion, HubSpot, Zoho and many databases. We confirm that your destination has a connection we can use before you order.
What if someone submits the form twice?
The Premium package checks for matching entries and flags or skips repeats, depending on your rule. Without that check, each submission is added as its own row.
Can I change the fields later?
Yes. Adding a field is small work, and our handover notes explain how. For bigger changes, you can order a small follow-up job.

desc:
Form to spreadsheet automation sends every contact, order or booking entry straight into the sheet, CRM or database where you work. Ecom Swift LLC connects your form, maps each answer to its column, tidies the formats and alerts your team.

## What does form to spreadsheet automation do?

It moves each form submission into a structured row without anyone copying it. When a visitor presses send, the answers are written into a Google Sheet, a CRM record or a database table, and a short alert tells the right person that something new has arrived. Uploaded files are saved to a folder and linked in the same row.

The idea is simple, but the details decide whether the data is usable: which answer goes in which column, how phone numbers are written, and what happens when the same person submits twice.

## The hidden cost of entries that sit in an inbox

Form notifications that land in a shared inbox look harmless. In practice they get read once, forgotten, and retyped later by whoever has time. Leads age, orders wait, and booking details are copied with small mistakes. Two people may answer the same enquiry, or nobody does because each assumes the other has it.

Entries kept only in email are also hard to count. You cannot filter them by date, sort them by source or ask how many requests came in last month. A sheet or CRM makes the same information searchable and ready for follow-up.

## How clean data changes your results

Speed and accuracy both improve. A new row appears the moment a form is sent, so the person who follows up sees the enquiry while the visitor is still thinking about it. Because answers go into fixed columns, nothing is lost in a long message, and nothing depends on a human reading an email correctly.

Clean formats matter more than they seem. Dates written the same way and phone numbers in a single pattern let you sort, filter and merge the data into mail tools or reports later. A duplicate check stops one customer from appearing three times, which keeps counts honest and avoids sending the same person repeated messages.

## What a great form connection includes

- A clear map from each form field to a named column.
- A new row for every submission, in the right sheet or tab.
- Phone, date and email formats cleaned on the way in.
- Dropdown and checkbox answers written in a readable form.
- Uploaded files stored in a folder with a link in the row.
- A timestamp and a source column, so you know where each entry came from.
- A team alert by email, with Slack or Teams as an option.
- A confirmation email to the person who submitted.
- A duplicate entry check.
- Routing by answer, so different requests reach different sheets.

## How we build it

First we look at your form and the places the data should go. We list every field, decide the column name and format for each, and note any answer that should trigger a different path, such as a sales enquiry versus a support request. Then we connect the form tool to the destination and send test entries through, including awkward ones with missing answers or very long text.

Basic connects one form to one sheet with an email alert. Standard connects two forms, writes to a sheet and a CRM, cleans formats and links uploaded files. Premium covers several forms, routing by answer, duplicate checks, a confirmation email and notes so you can add new forms yourself.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Keep the form short, so people finish it.
- Use dropdowns where the answers are a fixed set.
- Name columns clearly before connecting anything.
- Tell us which answers count as urgent.
- Test the form yourself after we finish.

**Avoid:**
- Renaming form fields after the connection is live without telling us.
- Using one free text box for several different pieces of information.
- Sending every alert to the whole team.
- Storing personal data in more places than you need.
- Editing the header row of the sheet that receives entries.

## Who it is for

A tradesperson who gets quote requests through a website form and wants them in a sheet with a phone number ready to call. A small online shop that takes custom order details and needs them in a tracking sheet. A studio with a booking form that must reach both a calendar sheet and a CRM.

## What we need from you

Share the link or export of your form, the destination sheet or CRM and a note about who should be alerted. Tell us what the columns should be called if you already have a preferred layout. We are added as a collaborator or team user in your accounts, we never ask for passwords, and you keep ownership of the forms, sheets and automations.
